01What the replay keeps true

Blueprint

A graph, not the world

Craft stores nodes and edge intent in one graph entity. While you edit it, specs stay ghosted: no task or real edge exists yet.

Gate

Approval lands first

The approval is a durable message on the graph thread. Only then does an orchestrating agent materialize entities and link them back.

Wave

Sessions are genuinely plural

Juniper and Callisto are separate work sessions from different providers. They work different nodes on the same graph while Dispatcher coordinates.

02Ref or spec

Node grammar stays lean. A ref points to something that exists. A spec gives the materializing agent enough intent to create something later.

Solid ink · existing 
{
  "id": "release-checklist",
  "ref": "01a09f…"
}
Ghost ink · to be born 
{
  "id": "invite-api",
  "spec": {
    "kind": "task",
    "title": "Harden invite API",
    "hint": "Validate the claim path"
  }
}

Sketch the job. A spec that reads like a finished task body is over-crafted.

03The plan stays attached

Materialization is agent-driven; the server does not walk the blueprint on its own. The agent creates real entities, wires real edges, and records links back to the graph.

  1. The graph row keeps the authored flow and its versions.
  2. The approval remains a message anchored to that graph.
  3. Spawned sessions and their working_on edges show who worked which node.
  4. Progress and steering messages stay on entity threads.

Truth noteCraft mode in chat and the Craft UI tab are one graph-authoring feature. Materialization happens through an agent and the delegation surface after approval; it is not an automatic server executor.
